:::{#hero-heading}

<br>

<div style="text-align: justify">
<p>I am a climate and atmospheric scientist dedicated to understanding the complex and rapidly evolving interactions between <strong>air quality</strong>, <strong>climate change</strong>, and <strong>cryospheric processes</strong> across the Hindu Kush Himalayan (HKH) region—one of the most climate‑sensitive and data‑scarce mountain systems on Earth. My research centers on the role of <strong> short‑lived climate pollutants</strong>, particularly <strong>black carbon</strong>, and how these particles influence regional climate dynamics, accelerate glacier melt, alter surface albedo, and modify radiative forcing patterns that ultimately affect downstream water resources and livelihoods.</p>

<p>To unravel these interconnected processes, I combine a diverse suite of modeling and observational approaches. My work spans <strong>general circulation models</strong>, <strong>regional climate models</strong>, <strong>radiative transfer simulations</strong>, <strong>radiation balance assessments</strong>, and <strong>hydrological modeling frameworks</strong>. These tools are complemented by <strong>ground‑based observations</strong>, <strong>satellite remote sensing</strong>, and <strong>high‑resolution gridded datasets</strong>, enabling a multi‑scale perspective that bridges atmospheric science, cryosphere research, and regional water‑balance studies. Through this integrated approach, I aim to generate actionable insights that support climate resilience, sustainable water management, and evidence‑based policy development across the HKH.</p>
</div>
